key_agent_trends: Coding agents advance to full PR lifecycle automation: review, fix, and policy-gated approvals.
Runtime security moves to agent-generated signed eBPF shields that protect live Linux systems without restarts.
MCP protocol gains production features for long-running tasks, mid-call elicitation, and server-provided skills.
Agentic commerce launches with controlled gateways, spending limits, and user approvals for retail purchases.
Regulators apply existing frameworks: firms stay accountable for agents; transactional actions may require authorisation.

stories.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Ship agents for PR review, fixes, and policy-based approvals
stories.what_happened: On 23 November 2026 Anthropic introduced Claude Ship in beta for Claude Team and Enterprise plans on GitHub. It bundles generally available Code Review with two beta agents: PR Steward (resolves failing CI, merge conflicts, and review feedback while commenting on changes and rollbacks) and Claude Approvals (approves routine changes against a plain-language policy file in the repository). Teams retain control via branch protection, spending limits, and observe mode. Internal data showed merged PRs more than doubling while reverts fell over 40% on Anthropic’s own Claude Code team.
stories.why_it_matters: It closes the gap between agent-written code and production shipping, potentially accelerating development velocity while keeping human policy and governance in the loop.

stories.headline: OpenAI and Cisco open-source Shirudo for AI-generated eBPF shields on live Linux
stories.what_happened: On 23 November 2026 OpenAI and Cisco released Shirudo, an open-source (BSD-2-Clause) Linux runtime based on eBPF. AI agents can write and load signed temporary shields that block exploit paths or replace vulnerable code on a running system without restart. A Codex-generated shield blocked a Java4Shell exploit against live Elasticsearch in testing. The project is pre-release, requires a patched kernel and TPM 2.0, and builds on Cisco’s Tetragon work.
stories.why_it_matters: It gives defenders a machine-speed temporary mitigation layer while permanent patches are tested and rolled out, addressing AI-accelerated vulnerability exploitation.

stories.headline: Anthropic enables Skills over MCP (beta), Tasks, and Elicitation (GA) in Claude
stories.what_happened: On 24 November 2026 Anthropic announced Skills over MCP in public beta, so MCP servers can publish skills (playbooks) that Claude loads only when needed. Tasks and Elicitation became generally available: Tasks allow servers to run long operations or agent loops while Claude continues work; Elicitation lets servers pause to request user input via forms or links. File Uploads is coming soon. Features are available for Pro/Max/Ultra and rolling out to Team/Enterprise. MCP reports over 700 million monthly SDK downloads and 10,000+ Claude connectors.
stories.why_it_matters: These protocol extensions make agents more capable of sustained, interactive, and guided multi-step work while keeping context lean and enabling human oversight at critical moments.

stories.headline: Walmart opens Agent Gateway so Meta’s Muse can shop Black Friday deals
stories.what_happened: Walmart made its Agent Gateway available to Meta’s Muse AI agent, enabling users to search products, build baskets, and complete purchases for Black Friday deals inside the Muse conversation. Shoppers set up Agent Profiles in their Walmart accounts with spending limits and approval rules. The agent does not receive purchase history or raw payment data; checkout uses saved cards under customer controls. The rollout occurred around 23–24 November after a brief same-day delay.
stories.why_it_matters: It is one of the first live, large-scale agent-to-retailer commerce integrations with explicit guardrails, testing whether controlled agent shopping can work at consumer scale.

stories.headline: UK FCA outlines when AI agents need authorisation for financial actions
stories.what_happened: On 24 November 2026 the UK Financial Conduct Authority published its approach to agentic AI in financial services. Agents that initiate payments, arrange credit, or make investment decisions may require authorisation regardless of who builds them. Regulated firms remain fully responsible for both in-house and third-party agents, including under Consumer Duty and the Senior Managers Regime. Technology providers are not exempt merely by calling themselves tech companies. No new AI-specific rules are planned; existing frameworks apply.
stories.why_it_matters: It clarifies the regulatory perimeter for agentic finance in a major market and signals that accountability stays with firms as agents move from information to transactions.

stories.headline: Sierra raises $1.75B Series F at $30B valuation for CX AI agents
stories.what_happened: On 23 November 2026 Sierra announced a $1.75 billion Series F led by Greenoaks and Lightspeed Venture Partners, with participation from Benchmark, Sequoia, GV, and Tiger Global. The round values the company at $30 billion, roughly double its valuation six months earlier. Sierra, co-founded by Bret Taylor, builds outcome-priced AI agents for enterprise customer experience and reports serving nearly half of the Fortune 50 with over $400 million ARR.
stories.why_it_matters: The rapid valuation jump and large raise underscore strong enterprise demand for production AI agents that resolve real customer outcomes rather than just chat.
